members.reason: Allocate needed resources (budgets, materials, tools) to research ventures — the shared lever is resource allocation.
Allocate financial resources (equipment, staff, expenses) for research — same allocation lever, same direction; interchangeable with the broader resources framing.
Citizen science: recruit the public into collecting and co-producing scientific knowledge — the core intervention.
Explicitly mediating academia to citizen science/volunteers to involve masses in the research process — same citizen-science participation intervention.
States the goal of the same convening ('הכינוס') — a discussion-and-agreement culture — i.e., a facet of the identical stakeholder-forum proposal.
Periodic convening of stakeholders representing diverse opinions to produce discussion and agreements — the core proposal, and it textually contains the other member.
Concrete proposal: researchers must involve end users and affected people in the research process.
'Combining knowledge and involvement for environmental change' is a vague slogan with no specific action — a general sentiment merged onto a concrete end-user-participation proposal.
Core: build understanding of the place through information layers and needs mapping.
'Information vacuum' is a problem statement, not a proposal — a problem merged with a solution violates the rubric.
Concrete proposal: give incentives and supports for carrying out the change.
'Connected to economic benefit' is a fragmentary observation about economic motivation, not the incentives-and-supports intervention — same topic, no shared specific action.
Simplify the problems into accessible, non-threatening, clear discourse tailored to different sectors — the audience-adapted-communication lever.
Speak in the target audience's language — the same audience-adapted-communication intervention, differing only in formulation.
Core: broad cross-disciplinary, cross-campus, cross-sector collaborations aimed at concrete impact.

Coordinating specifically with the local authority to align ventures with community needs is a narrower, different action (legitimacy/alignment with one actor) than the broad multi-axis collaboration portfolio — same topic, different scope and lever.
Deepen knowledge across trans-disciplines and seek solutions in diverse directions — the cross-disciplinary research lever.
Promote multidisciplinary research combining social science, exact sciences and technology — the same cross-disciplinary intervention.
Concrete proposal: map existing knowledge sources (prior research, data) as a base for research-field collaboration.
'Successful collaboration' is a two-word sentiment with no action at all — a value statement merged with a concrete mapping proposal.
Personal acquaintance with someone who researched and understands the topic — the direct-personal-connection lever.
Personal acquaintance as the key, via conferences emphasizing unmediated connection — same intervention with the venue named.
A connecting agent who clarifies research data and makes the interpersonal connection — the brokered-connection lever between researchers and change actors.
'Matchmaking' researchers with civil-society orgs and ministries is the same brokered-connection intervention, same direction.
Concrete proposal: physical meetings between academics and practitioners as a knowledge-sharing platform.

'Connecting people is critical, promote initiatives that bring different-minded people together' is a general value statement with no specific mechanism (not necessarily physical, not academia-practitioner) — sentiment merged with a concrete proposal.
Provide funding and operational latitude to enable implementing ideas and cross-sector collaborations — the resource-provision lever.
Provide resources and options (information access, tools, budgets, workshops) supporting academia-practitioner collaboration — the same resource-provision intervention.
Interpersonal relationships as the bridge between research and the field, clarifying data — the sustained-personal-ties lever.
Long-term personal ties between research representatives and the field, built via meetings and workshops — the same sustained-personal-ties intervention.
Significant motivation, patience and persistence through a long change process — the perseverance lever.
Stubbornness: consistency and commitment through the research process despite challenges — interchangeable with the persistence formulation.
Core: proper dosage between scientific validity and activist passion (as demonstrated in successful environmental struggles).

Combining environmental emotion with a sense of self-efficacy pairs different components — no scientific-validity element, efficacy instead — same emotional-drivers topic but a different combination/lever.
'Research can drive big things' is a value/sentiment statement with no proposed action — merged onto concrete applied-research proposals.
Core: strengthen applied research so research contributes to changing reality.

Developing scientific tools to underpin solutions/policy change is a distinct concrete action (build tools) rather than strengthening applied research generally — same direction, different intervention.
Make research practical and implementable rather than theoretical — interchangeable with strengthening applied research.
Establish partnerships with academic institutions, social organizations and businesses to leverage joint knowledge and resources — the cross-sector-partnership lever.
Recruit committed, influential partners from the first stages — same partnership intervention; the early-timing emphasis is formulation, not a different lever.
Build collaborations between academia, industry and social organizations to drive research projects — the same cross-sector-partnership intervention.

A general appeal to systemic thinking, mutual support and collaboration between actors — its added lever (systemic thinking) and generic framing are not the specific visionary-executor pairing; general principle merged with a concrete proposal.
Core concrete proposal: collaborations pairing vision/ideology holders with executors who implement plans.
